stacks.why: Text has a hidden-cause twist (it's the waiting, not referrals) in 9 words; spoken gives the vivid moment (sign three, then wait) in 10 words. The spoken line does not say 'empty months' as the text does, so the two claims are close but not the same, and the text carries the whole promise.

The flip of a misread is clear and the two channels match. But the line is only 6 words (short of the 8 to 14 spoken target), names no buyer, moment or cause, and gives no reason to keep watching. Sound-off the reader cannot tell who it is for. Text and spoken are identical, so nothing is added.

Spoken is strong: a countable failed fix (doubled your cold emails) then the cause, in 11 words. The text never says cold email or outreach, so sound-off it does not lock the buyer; it only says 'no replies'. The 'first line, not volume' contrast is good.

Spoken matches the text's 'empty months' with a feast-or-famine contrast (three clients, then literally nothing). It is specific, plain and in the buyer's words; 'literally' is a minor filler. Text is the same as S01 and carries the hidden-cause twist.

Text names the feast-famine pattern but only denies the cause ('referrals aren't the problem'), with no reason or surprise promised, so it is weaker than S01 and S04. Spoken is the same vivid line as S01 and carries the stack.

'Your kidneys' breaks the meta check, 'crying for help' is a generic fear line, and foam is claimed as a kidney signal with no brand-owned fact. The spoken line opens with a character setup in 18 words and states the problem late. The foam moment is vivid and in the buyer's words, which keeps it at C and not lower.
